# nish/net/serve

An HTTP/1.1 server for an `async` program: one task and one region per request, answers in request order.

```ts
import {
  Request,
  Response,
  ServeLimits,
  ServeStats,
  refuse,
  serve,
  serveOn,
} from "nish/net/serve";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { Request, Response, ServeLimits, refuse, serve } from "nish/net/serve"
import { Router, RouterLimits } from "nish/net/router"
import { sleep } from "nish:async"

const HOME: i32 = 0   // module constants, in the order the routes are added
const USER: i32 = 1

async function handle(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
  switch (req.route) {
    case HOME: return new Response(200).text("hello\n")
    case USER: {
      await sleep(5)   // a database, another service: the loop runs on
      return new Response(200).json(`{"id":"${req.param(0)}"}`)
    }
    default: return refuse(req)   // 404, or 405 with its Allow
  }
}

export async function main(): Promise<i32> {
  const router = new Router(new RouterLimits())
  router.add("GET", "/")
  router.add("GET", "/users/:id")
  return await serve(8080, router, new ServeLimits(), handle)
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="refuse" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#refuse">

The answer for a request the router refused: 405 with an `Allow` field naming the methods the path has, and 404 for anything else.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="serve" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#serve">

Serves HTTP/1.1 on `port` on every address, handing each request to `handle` in a task of its own, until `limits.maxRequests` are answered (for good when it is 0).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="serve​On" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#serveon">

`serve` on a listening socket the program made — `tcpListen` on port 0 in a test, or `tcpListenFlags` with SO_REUSEPORT for a worker — filling `stats` as it runs.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Request" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#request">

A request, as `handle` reads it: the task's own copy of the head and body, valid for as long as the task runs.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Response" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#response">

The answer `handle` gives: a status, a content type and a body.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Serve​Limits" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#servelimits">

The caps a server holds every request and connection to; each field is read once, by `serve`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

`serve` runs `nish/net/handler`'s readiness loop as an `async` function:
it awaits the loop's descriptor, so the program's other tasks run while no
socket is ready. Each whole request it takes is handed to `handle` in a
task of its own, spawned with the request's slot, and the task's
allocations — the request it reads, the response it builds, whatever the
handler makes on the way — live in the task's region and go when it ends.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="The task reads its own copy">

The task copies the request's head and
body out of the server's slot into its own memory before `handle` runs,
and when `handle` answers it writes the status, the content type and the
body back into the slot's fixed buffers, element by element, and wakes the
loop. The loop then sends the answer and frees the slot. Nothing the task
allocated outlives it, and the loop's arena does not grow per request once
its slots are warm: `tests/link/net_serve_pipelined_flat` pins
`Arena.used()` flat over thousands of pipelined requests. What the runtime
allocates outside the arena for a task and its region is not measured.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Answers keep request order">

The handler reads a connection's next
request only once the one before it is answered, so at most one request
per connection is in flight, and pipelined requests are answered in the
order they came: a later request's task starts only after the earlier one
is answered, so it can never finish first.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Every cap answers.** `ServeLimits` bounds the connections, the requests
in flight (503 past it), a request's header section (431) and body (413),
and the response a task may write (500 past it). `docs/security/serve.md`
is the record.

</scalar-callout>

`readable` is refused under `--emit-ts` (NL4017), so a program that serves
is native only.

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

## Functions

### refuse

The answer for a request the router refused: 405 with an `Allow` field
naming the methods the path has, and 404 for anything else.

```ts
function refuse(_req: Request): Response
```

<scalar-field name="_req" type="Request" required>

the request to refuse; the loop answers it from the request it holds

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Response">

a response the server answers as `HttpHandler.refuse` does

</scalar-field>

### serve

Serves HTTP/1.1 on `port` on every address, handing each request to
`handle` in a task of its own, until `limits.maxRequests` are answered (for
good when it is 0).

```ts
function serve(
  port: i32,
  router: Router,
  limits: ServeLimits,
  handle: (req: Request) => Promise<Response>,
): Promise<i32>
```

<scalar-field name="port" type="i32" required>

the TCP port to listen on

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="router" type="Router" required>

the routes, added before the call; a request's `route` is the index `Router.add` answered

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="limits" type="ServeLimits" required>

the caps; see `ServeLimits`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="handle" type="(req: Request) =&gt; Promise&lt;Response&gt;" required>

the program's answer to a request, run as its own task

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;i32&gt;">

0 once stopped, or the negative error `tcpListen` answered

</scalar-field>

### serveOn

`serve` on a listening socket the program made — `tcpListen` on port 0 in
a test, or `tcpListenFlags` with SO_REUSEPORT for a worker — filling
`stats` as it runs.

```ts
function serveOn(
  listener: i32,
  router: Router,
  limits: ServeLimits,
  handle: (req: Request) => Promise<Response>,
  stats: ServeStats,
): Promise<i32>
```

<scalar-field name="listener" type="i32" required>

the listening socket, still the program's to close

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="router" type="Router" required>

the routes, added before the call

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="limits" type="ServeLimits" required>

the caps; see `ServeLimits`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="handle" type="(req: Request) =&gt; Promise&lt;Response&gt;" required>

the program's answer to a request, run as its own task

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="stats" type="ServeStats" required>

where the server counts what it did, the caller's

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;i32&gt;">

0 once stopped

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### Request

A request, as `handle` reads it: the task's own copy of the head and body,
valid for as long as the task runs.

```ts
class Request
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Request(raw: HttpRequest)` | A request over `raw`, which it keeps. |
| `raw: HttpRequest` | The request as the handler parsed it, copied into the task: its spans, its head and its body. |
| `route: i32` | The index `Router.add` answered for the route, or a negative `ROUTER_*` code. |
| `header(name: string): string` | The value of the first header field named `name`. |
| `method(): string` | The method. |
| `param(k: i32): string` | Route parameter `k`, percent-decoded. Panics when the request's route has no parameter `k`. |
| `paramMalformed(k: i32): boolean` | Whether route parameter `k` holds a malformed percent escape, which a program answers 400. Panics when the request's route has no parameter `k`. |
| `paramNumber(k: i32): i32` | Route parameter `k` read as a decimal number that is not negative and fits an `i32`. Panics when the request's route has no parameter `k`. |
| `path(): string` | The path: the target up to its `?`, still percent-encoded. |
| `query(name: string): string` | The first query parameter named `name`, form-decoded (`+` as a space, `%XX` as its byte). |
| `text(): string` | The body as text. |

### Response

The answer `handle` gives: a status, a content type and a body. Build it
with `new Response(status)` and one of `text`, `json` or `bytes`, or with
`refuse`.

```ts
class Response
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Response(status: i32)` | An answer with `status` and no body yet. |
| `body: u8[]` | The body, `body[0 .. length)`. |
| `length: i32` | How many bytes of `body` are the body. |
| `status: i32` | The status, from 200 to 599; any other is answered 500. |
| `type: string` | The `Content-Type` value; empty sends none, and the body goes without one. |
| `bytes(type: string, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): Response` | Sets a body of bytes with a content type. |
| `json(s: string): Response` | Sets a JSON body the program wrote. |
| `text(s: string): Response` | Sets a plain-text body. |

### ServeLimits

The caps a server holds every request and connection to; each field is read once, by `serve`.

```ts
class ServeLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ServeLimits()` |  |
| `bodyBytes: i32` | The most bytes a request body may have; past it the request is answered 413 and its connection ends. |
| `connections: i32` | The most connections open at once; a connection past it is accepted and closed at once, and its client sees the connection reset. |
| `deadline: i32` | Milliseconds a request's task may run, from its start to its answer; past it the task is cancelled: each await it is parked on, and each it makes later, answers false at once, so it runs to its end and its slot is freed. 0 or less sets no limit. |
| `headerBytes: i32` | The most bytes a request's header section may have; past it the request is answered 431 and its connection ends. |
| `headTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds a connection may take to send a whole request head, from its first byte; past it the connection is closed. The bound on a client that trickles its head (slowloris): it holds a connection this long, no longer. |
| `idleTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds a connection may go without a byte read or written, as a keep-alive connection does between requests; past it the connection is closed, freeing its slot. |
| `inFlight: i32` | The most requests in flight — handed to a task and not yet answered — at once; past it a request is answered 503. |
| `maxRequests: i32` | How many requests to answer before stopping: the server then stops accepting, finishes what it holds and returns. 0, the default, serves for good. |
| `responseBytes: i32` | The most bytes a response body may have; a task that answers more is answered 500 instead. |

### ServeStats

What a server did, for a log line or a test; `serveOn` fills it as it runs.

```ts
class ServeStats
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ServeStats()` |  |
| `answered: i32` | Requests answered, by a task or by the server itself. |
| `busy: i32` | Requests answered 503 because `inFlight` tasks were already running. |
| `failed: i32` | Answers a task wrote that broke a cap or a rule, answered 500 instead. |
| `slots: i32` | How many slots the server made: the most requests ever in flight at once. |
| `usedEnd: i64` | `Arena.used()` in the server's loop once `maxRequests` were answered, before draining. |
| `usedWarm: i64` | `Arena.used()` in the server's loop once `warmAfter` requests were answered. |
| `warmAfter: i32` | After how many answers to read `usedWarm`; 0 reads it never. |
